port.label: Heat pump port
port.help: Standard Native TCP: 8889 (For very old V1.x firmwares: 8888)

infoInterval.text: ⚠️ Tip: Do not set the polling interval too low! Frequent requests put a heavy load on the heat pump's CPU, making the controller very sluggish. Recommended: 30-60 seconds.

options.label: 🔒 Read-Only (Monitoring only – 0% flash wear, all optimizations disabled)
✍️ Read & Write: Without Modbus (Native via Port 8889 – writes to EEPROM)
⚡ Read & Write: With Modbus TCP (Hybrid – wear-free RAM access)

infoModeReadonly.text: 🔒 Read-Only Mode active: The adapter only reads telemetry and parameters. All write-related tabs (Modbus, Idle Defaults, Cycle Optimization, HUP, ZIP, PV Surplus) are disabled and grayed out. Manual changes in the object tree are blocked.

infoModeNative.text: ✍️ Write Mode (Without Modbus / Native Port 8889): Active optimizations and parameter changes are written directly to the Luxtronik EEPROM via port 8889. Please enable 'Idle Defaults' when using optimizations and monitor daily flash write cycles.

infoModeModbus.text: ⚡ Hybrid Mode (Write with Modbus TCP): Volatile parameters (setpoints, offsets, coils) are written directly into the controller's RAM via Modbus TCP without causing EEPROM flash wear. Please select your active registers in the 'Modbus (Hybrid)' tab.

infoLanguage.text:
Select the language in which operating states and statuses should be displayed in the ioBroker object tree.

Example:

text.en:
Hybrid Mode: Modbus TCP
Use Modbus TCP to write volatile parameters (like target temperatures or SmartGrid) directly into the RAM without causing wear to the EEPROM flash memory. Sensor data is still reliably read via the native port 8889.
text.de:
Hybrid-Modus: Modbus TCP
Nutze Modbus TCP, um flüchtige Parameter (wie PV-Sollwerte oder SmartGrid) direkt in den Arbeitsspeicher zu schreiben, ohne den EEPROM-Flashspeicher der Anlage zu verschleißen. Sensordaten werden weiterhin detailliert über den nativen Port 8889 gelesen.

informationIdle.text:
⚠️ Flash Memory Protection
To prevent EEPROM/flash wear on your Luxtronik controller, parameters are only updated during active optimizations. Once the heat pump returns to idle, all modified parameters are automatically reverted to your defined default values below to ensure a safe operating state.

💡 Recommendation: It is highly recommended to enable this feature if you use the intelligent cycle optimization (hot water + heating) and/or the dynamic HUP control!

heatCurveCredit.text: 💡 Note: A big thank you to mnemotron.de for the inspiration for this visual heat curve diagram!

confirm.text: Please ensure you fill in ALL default values correctly below. Empty or wrong values can disrupt your heating system!

text.en: Calculate the Coefficient of Performance (COP / JAZ) of your heat pump over various timeframes (24h, 7d, 1m, 1y). You can use the internal heat pump meters or link accurate external smart meters (e.g. Shelly 3EM).
text.de: Berechne die Arbeitszahl (COP / JAZ) deiner Wärmepumpe über verschiedene Zeiträume (Heute, 7 Tage, Monat, Jahr). Du kannst dafür die internen Schätzwerte der Anlage nutzen oder hochpräzise externe Zähler (z.B. Shelly 3EM) verlinken.

informationCycleOptimization.text:
By default, the Luxtronik controller treats heating and domestic hot water (DHW) cycles as separate operations. This adapter coordinates both runs so the compressor transitions seamlessly without unnecessary stop/start cycles.

➔ Trigger rule: If (DHW Target - DHW Actual) ≥ (DHW Hysteresis - 1.5 K), Heating Return ≤ Return Target, heating is enabled (no heating limit/off/vacation), and DHW is allowed within the next 25 minutes (no lock time), heating is gently pre-started by temporarily raising the heating parallel offset by Heating Hysteresis + 0.5 K (automatically reset once the compressor runs stably).

confirm.title: Important Recommendation
confirm.text: You are activating the intelligent cycle optimization. It is highly recommended to also enable 'Force default values during idle' in the 'Idle Defaults' tab! This ensures that the heat pump returns to a safe state after the adapter intervenes.

infoHup.text:
Dynamic voltage control for controllable 0–10V heating circulating pumps (HUP). (Note: PWM pumps are automatically detected and bypassed).

⚠️ Important Prerequisites:
1. Hardware Check: Only enable this if your pump is actually controlled via an analog 0-10V signal from the Luxtronik controller. If your system is configured for PWM, the adapter will automatically detect this and safely disable the regulation.
2. System Types: The ideal spread depends entirely on your heating system. Underfloor heating (FBH) typically requires 3 to 5 K, whereas traditional radiators often run optimally between 7 to 10 K.
3. Voltage Scale: Ensure you select the correct hardware multiplier for your firmware version below.

hup_voltage_factor.label: Hardware voltage scale
hup_voltage_factor.help: Select 100 for V2.x (1000 = 10.0V). Select 10 for V3.x (100 = 10.0V).

confirm.title: Important Recommendation
confirm.text: You are activating dynamic pump control. It is highly recommended to also enable 'Force default values during idle' in the 'Idle Defaults' tab! This ensures your pump returns to its safe baseline voltage when the heating cycle finishes.

zip_control_mode.label: How is your circulation pump (ZIP) controlled?

infoController.text: ⚠️ Note: Controlling via the Luxtronik causes write operations (wear) on the internal flash memory. Set 'Disable base ZIP values' to false if the relay is powered by the heat pump directly.

infoActor.text: ✅ Recommended: The Luxtronik output is permanently disabled. The adapter controls your relay via Wi-Fi (0% wear). Please configure your external relays below.

infoModbus.text: ℹ️ Hybrid: The pump is controlled via Modbus Coil 7 without flash wear. Requires active Modbus setting.

zip_lWP_aktiv.label: Disable base ZIP values (Set Luxtronik timers to 0)

pv_info_header.text: How it works: PV Surplus Control

pv_info_desc.text: Automatically raises the setpoints for hot water and heating when your solar system feeds enough power into the grid. The adapter waits for active cycles to finish before reverting values to protect the compressor.

pv_battery_active.label: Include battery charging power (Prioritize Heat Pump)

pv_wp_power_active.label: Include current heat pump power consumption
pv_wp_power_active.help: Adds the heat pump's own power draw to the net PV balance so an already running cycle does not cancel out the PV surplus.

pv_sunset_cutoff_active.label: Block new boost before sunset
pv_sunset_cutoff_active.help: Prevents starting a new PV boost shortly before sunset using your ioBroker system coordinates.

pv_sunset_buffer.label: Buffer before sunset (Minutes)
pv_sunset_buffer.help: No new PV boost will be started within this time window before local sunset.

pv_finish_cycle.label: Finish active cycle to base target after reset
pv_finish_cycle.help: If deactivated, the compressor might stop immediately if current temp is higher than base target.

backupInfo.text:
You can download the heat pump's internal logs (.dta) directly via its web interface.

💡 Tip: To graphically analyze the .dta files on your PC, we recommend the free tool OpenDTA (<a href='https://sourceforge.net/projects/opendta/').

• Live DTA (/NewProc): Generates a fresh log right now.
• Existing DTA (/proclog): Downloads the last auto-saved log (can be 2-3 hours old).

autoBackupActive.label: Enable automatic DTA download
autoBackupActive.help: If enabled, the adapter will automatically download the DTA log according to the schedule and save it to the ioBroker file system.

backupLocationInfo.text: Automated DTA backups are safely stored in the global ioBroker file system. You can find them in the main ioBroker menu under 'Files' in the folder 0_userdata.0.luxtronik_backups. From there, you can easily download them to your PC and analyze them using tools like OpenDTA.
